interest: American firms lobby through the China-America Council to reform China's 1935 Trademark Law at the end of the war.
keywords: China-America Council of Commerce and Industry
overview: This file comprises correspondence and legal memoranda from late 1944 and early 1945 between the China-America Council of Commerce and Industry, the U.S. Department of State's Office of Far Eastern Affairs, and the Department of Commerce concerning proposed revisions to Chinese intellectual property legislation. A. Viola Smith, Washington Representative of the Council, transmitted to Deputy Director Edwin F. Stanton a detailed proposal drafted by international trademark authority Dr. Stephen P. Ladas alongside member commentary recommending amendments to the Chinese Trade-Mark Law of November 23, 1935, as well as a memorandum on China's new patent law. The proposed amendments advocate broadening trademark protections to ideographic concepts and pronunciations, protecting prior users against piracy, easing rigid assignment and non-user cancellation rules, establishing robust civil remedies including temporary injunctions, protecting unregistered trade names, prohibiting unfair competition, and restoring Allied trademark rights suspended during the war with Japan.

subfiles.about: Detailed draft proposals and legal commentary by the China-America Council recommending extensive revisions to China's 1935 Trademark Law.
subfiles.from: China-America Council of Commerce and Industry, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Prepared by Dr. Stephen P. Ladas and the Sub-Committee on Trade-Marks, Copyrights and Patents, this memorandum presents draft revisions and explanatory commentary across five major areas of Chinese trademark legislation. It proposes expanding trademark protection to encompass pronunciation and ideographic concepts, protecting prior users against unauthorized registration, liberalizing strict assignment recording deadlines and five-year non-use forfeiture rules, and allowing multiple goods groups per application. The memorandum also urges adding strong penal and civil remedies including temporary injunctions, protecting unregistered commercial trade names, establishing explicit safeguards against unfair competition, and restoring trademark rights disrupted by the war for one year following the end of hostilities with Japan.
subfiles.title: Draft of Amendments to the Chinese Trade-Mark Law of November 23, 1935

subfiles.about: Supplementary comments from Council members critiquing and evaluating specific aspects of the draft trademark amendments.
subfiles.from: Members of the China-America Council of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.summary: Council members' late comments of November 1944 on the draft trademark amendments, chiefly urging that only 'confusingly similar' marks be barred.
subfiles.title: Additional Comments from Council Members Received After Memo Mimeographed
